reason: The provided sources contain ample overlapping facts about the LISA space mission to construct a verified 45-second script with more than 10 multi-sourced claims.
story: Imagine a telescope in space so massive its arms stretch 1.6 million miles across the void—wider than the Sun itself. This is LISA, the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, a planned European Space Agency mission scheduled to launch in 2035 aboard an Ariane 6 rocket. Composed of three spacecraft flying in a giant triangular formation following Earth, LISA acts as the first dedicated space-based gravitational-wave observatory. As invisible ripples in spacetime—generated by colliding supermassive black holes and dead stars—wash over the solar system, they subtly squeeze and stretch the distance between the spacecraft. By bouncing lasers between free-floating gold-platinum cubes, LISA will measure these cosmic tremors with a jaw-dropping precision smaller than the width of a single helium atom. By breaking free from the seismic noise of Earth, this colossal space antenna will open an entirely new window to listen to the dark universe.
angle: A planned space detector featuring three spacecraft separated by 1.6 million miles—wider than the Sun—designed to measure spacetime ripples smaller than an atom.

claims.claim: LISA is a planned European Space Agency space mission to detect and measure gravitational waves.
The mission consists of three spacecraft flying in an equilateral triangle formation.
Each side of the triangular constellation is 2.5 million kilometres (1.6 million miles) long.
The spacecraft will follow or trail Earth in a heliocentric orbit around the Sun.
Launch is planned for approximately 2035 aboard an Ariane 6 launch vehicle.
Each spacecraft carries free-floating test masses made of gold-platinum cubes.
LISA will use laser interferometry to measure changes in distance smaller than the diameter of a helium atom.
Potential sources for signals include merging supermassive black holes at the centre of galaxies.
ESA formally adopted the LISA mission on January 25, 2024.
NASA is participating as a collaborative partner providing key components such as lasers and telescopes.
The underlying measurement technology was successfully demonstrated in space by the LISA Pathfinder mission.
OHB System AG signed an agreement with ESA in 2025 to build the spacecraft.

disputed: Exact historical development timelines and the precise impact of varying US administration budgets on NASA's hardware contributions are viewed with fluctuating certainty across sources; scripts should focus on current official partnership agreements and the confirmed 2035 launch timeline.
